detail.longDescription: Hey HN, I'm Jakob, the solo dev and founder behind Taskless. I got tired of my AGENTS.md files being ignored or forgotten a half dozen turns into conversations. I also remembered reading someone here on HN saying we weren't using nearly enough syntax trees in our code checks. This is the result. Taskless gives you powerful syntax tree tools with human verifiable fixtures. The CLI is MIT licensed, so running the CLI, onboarding, rule writing, and running the underlying ast-grep & Vale checks are all local. You can give it a try with: npx @taskless/cli and then asking your agent to "onboard with Taskless". Under the hood, the CLI works with your agent to read your PR review comments, fixup commits, and agent files. It takes things that keep recurring and turns them into the simplest code-level enforcement that can prevent the issue going forward. By choosing code over an LLM for the runtime, there's no model once code is generated. The checks can then be committed to your codebase and enforced. I'm particularly proud of how determinism is mixed into the onboarding flow. Any time the CLI can give the agent information without letting the agent wandering the codebase, the CLI does. It results in a more consistent experience with far fewer errors. Anonymous telemetry can be disabled outright by setting DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or TASKLESS_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 in your environment (it collects CLI version, OS, the repo's org/owner, and a bit about the repository it's running in). When the agent's done, it creates a report you can share around to show everyone there's a better way to control the output of agentic coding tools. I thought I'd include a few here from some of my favorite repos. - Effect: https://tskl.es/gh/Effect-TS/effect/20261104/1g4gRoMmoADlysg... I specifically liked Effect because effect-bot is in the PRs fixing bugs and writing docs for the team, and they already use oxlint plugins and a TypeScript language service plugin. - Sentry: https://tskl.es/gh/getsentry/sentry/20261016/1ZyMPva1BzaHaa5... Sentry's all open source, and David Cramer's tweeted a lot about determinism, especially now that the team is using Junior to ship code via Slack chat. - n8n: https://tskl.es/gh/n8n-io/n8n/20261026/1C3I3yVjFyfxNFEpl4qFA... n8n has more AI driven code than the other two repos and is a good example of how bad it can get when the determinism isn't in place. Since agents tend to copy what they see from related files, problems propagate quickly. I'd love to hear what you're doing today to keep agents behaving, or if you do kick the tires, I'd love the honest feedback.
